tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Choose connected job sources or Open web search (web), alone or together. For web, the MCP returns a requires_host_search request; the assistant must execute it using its own native web search, verify live listings and cite their real URLs. If native web search is unavailable, report that limitation; never treat the handoff as completed search or zero matches. Web results do not have MCP job IDs and cannot use get_job or open_application_link. Use the MCP for the six connected sources instead of browsing them separately. Search only the agreed sources. If unclear, ask: Hidden Jobs only, or all available sources? Do not enumerate external platforms in that question. Offer only these two choices. All available sources means hiddenjobs, every integrated external provider and web. Honor explicit narrower selections or exclusions and reuse an agreed selection. sources is required and must not be empty. External offers and their source links are free; Hidden Jobs original application links are included. limit applies per source. Inspect sourceResults for failures, coverage and continuation cursors; never treat a failed source as no jobs. Present one unified ranked list with the same format for every source: linked title, short summary, confirmed remote location, published salary or a clearly labelled cited market estimate and a verified Apply link. Never group by platform or add platform-specific introductions. Keep source IDs internal and required provider credits with the listing link. Never invent an application URL; a detail-only link must be labelled View job. After presenting results, first offer a daily search through the assistant’s native scheduler if it supports unattended MCP calls; load get_workflow search for scheduling guidance. Preserve sources, filters and the selected profile/CV; notify about new relevant matches. Verify scheduler support and user approval before creating a task; never claim a reminder can run searches. If unavailable or the user prefers email, offer Hidden Jobs-only alerts with approval. Offer saved-CV matching when that is the more useful next step.

sources.description: Required selection; no default. hiddenjobs only selects Hidden Jobs. All available sources selects hiddenjobs, jobicy, weworkremotely, remoteok, himalayas, itjobs and web. Respect explicit subsets or exclusions. web uses the assistant’s own web search; it is not a provider API.

cursors.description: Pass a sourceResults.nextCursor unchanged for the same source and filters. page applies to Hidden Jobs; external feeds use these cursors.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Read a job from its original source using the source and id returned by search_jobs. External details are rechecked through the public provider API/feed. Hidden Jobs original application URLs remain excluded.

tools.name: open_application_link
tools.description: Open the supplied source link for an external offer for free. For Hidden Jobs, reveal the original application URL. Pass the source and id returned by search_jobs; never replace external source links with employer links. Before ending a tailored-CV handoff, offer to save a named reusable CV version in Hidden Jobs if not already saved. Offer tracking only for Hidden Jobs applications; do not mark submitted from opening this link.

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
